'''''Campanula persicifolia''''', the '''peach-leaved bellflower''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a [[flowering plant]] [[species]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Campanulaceae]]. It is an [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] growing to {{convert|1|m|0|abbr=on}}.<ref name=dvf>{{cite web |url=http://linnaeus.nrm.se/flora/di/campanula/campa/campper.html |title=Campanula persicifolia |last1=Anderberg |first1=Arne |last2=Anderberg |first2=Anna-Lena |work=Den virtuella floran |publisher=[[Swedish Museum of Natural History]] |language=Swedish |accessdate=27 November 2010}}</ref> Its [[flower]]s are cup-shaped and can be either lilac-blue or white.<ref name="perennials">Susan Carter, Carrie Becker, Bob Lilly: ''Perennials: The Gardener's reference'', page 123. Timber Press, 2007</ref> Its [[foliage]] is narrow and glossy with a bright green appearance.<ref name="perennials"/>

It is widely considered an English cottage garden classic.<ref name="Iannotti">{{cite web |last1=Iannotti |first1=Marie |title=12 Best Plants For An English Garden |url=https://www.thespruce.com/english-garden-plants-4174047 |website=The Spruce |access-date=12 June 2021}}</ref><ref name="Geets">{{cite web |last1=Geets |first1=Sheryl |title=Low Maintenance Cottage Garden Plants |url=https://www.bhg.com/gardening/design/styles/best-plants-for-cottage-gardens/ |website=Better Homes & Gardens |access-date=12 June 2021}}</ref>

==Description==
''Campanula persicifolia'' is a clump-forming [[perennial plant|perennial]] [[herbaceous plant]] growing to a height of {{convert|30|to|100|cm}}. The stem is usually unbranched, erect and slightly angular. The basal leaves are  short stalked and narrowly spatulate and usually wither before flowering time. The upper leaves are unstalked, lanceolate, almost linear with rounded teeth on the margins. The [[inflorescence]] is a few-flowered terminal [[raceme]] or there may be a single flower. The calyx is fused with five narrow lobes, eventually spreading. The corolla is five-lobed, {{convert|30|to|50|mm|1|abbr=on}} long with five violet-blue (or occasionally white) fused petals. The corolla lobes are less long than they are wide. There are five stamens and a pistil formed from three fused carpels. The fruit is a strongly-veined conical capsule. The flowering period is from June to August.<ref name=NatureGate>{{cite web |url=http://www.luontoportti.com/suomi/en/kukkakasvit/peach-leaved-bellflower |title=Peach-leaved Bellflower: ''Campanula persicifolia'' |publisher=NatureGate |accessdate=2013-12-31}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Campanula persicifolia'' is common in the Alps and other mountain ranges in Europe. It grows at lower altitudes in the north, and higher up further south, passing {{convert|1500|m|0|abbr=on}} in Provence. Normally it flowers in June; a dry summer may reduce or inhibit its flowering. Despite this it can flower as late as September in a cold year. The natural habitat of this plant is broad-leaved forests, woodland margins, rocky outcrops in broad-leaved woods, meadows and banks.<ref name=NatureGate/>

==Cultivation==
In cultivation numerous [[variety (botany)|varieties]] and [[cultivar]]s have been developed in a range of colours including white, blue, pink and purple.<ref>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>
